title: Late-binding log mapper with observable error tags and flow control
creator: Marco Rivera
description:
Problem: Our current ingress pipeline performs eager schema binding and field normalization at the edge, which causes: 1) frequent rejections for polymorphic payloads, 2) loss of high-cardinality debugging fields due to coarse sanitization rules, and 3) spikes in CPU when many tenants send slightly varying event shapes. This makes tracing joins brittle and increases MTTI for customer incidents.

Proposal: Implement a late-binding log mapper that: (a) accepts polymorphic JSON-lines at the edge and stores a small canonical envelope (tenant, timestamp, raw_payload_ref, provisional_correlation_id), (b) runs an asynchronous, per-tenant mapping worker that applies tenant-configured field mappings, enrichment (trace linking, span-affinity), and cost-aware deduplication, and (c) emits a canonical structured_event into Loki/ELK with stable correlation_id and observable error tags when mapping fails. The pipeline must support backpressure (circuit to drop/aggregate low-value fields when overloaded), opt-in tenant sampling for raw payload retention, and debugging hooks to reconstruct raw->canonical transformations for postmortems.
acceptance_criteria: Edge agent emits envelope with provisional_correlation_id and reference to raw payload store for >=99% of ingested events
Asynchronous mapper transforms polymorphic payloads into canonical structured_event for 95% of common tenant schemas in test corpus
When mapping fails, structured_event contains observable error.tag fields (mapping_error_type, mapping_rule_id) and original provisional_correlation_id
Pipeline scales to sustained 6k events/sec per region with tail latency of async mapper < 200ms under normal load
Backpressure mode engages when mapper queue > 80% and drops non-essential high-cardinality fields while preserving correlation IDs
End-to-end tests and a canary run show no increase in 5xx ingestion errors for top-20 customers
Documentation and runbooks updated; rollout plan executed with monitoring dashboards and rollback threshold set
tasks: Design: finalize envelope schema and retention TTL for raw payload store (S3/Cold Blob)
Proto: implement edge agent change to emit envelope and provisional_correlation_id
Service: implement async mapper service with tenant config store and plugin points for enrichment hooks
Integrations: add mapping_error tags to Loki labels and Elastic ingest pipeline mapping
Backpressure: implement queue-length based circuit to switch to compact mode (drop fields)
Testing: generate polymorphic test corpus from customer logs and run mapping accuracy job
Observability: create mapping success/failure metrics, queue-length histograms and dashboard panels
Rollout: canary to 5% of traffic, then 25%, 50%, 100% with rollback gates
comments: 2026-03-10 Marco Rivera: Initial ticket created after postmortem for high-ingest CPU spike. Proposed late-binding approach to reduce edge work and make mapping pluggable.
2026-03-11 Priya Desai (PM): Suggest exposing tenant-config UI in Console for mapping rules and retention opt-in. Will partner with UX.

2026-03-12 Aisha Khan: Prototype of envelope produced. Using provisional_correlation_id as sha1(tenant+raw_sha+ingest_ts) to ensure determinism. Putting raw payloads into cold blob with 7d TTL by default.

2026-03-13 Security review note (Jake Lin): raw_payload retention must be opt-in; default redaction at ingestion for PII. Added security_review_required=false for now but will create follow-up if tenants request retention.

2026-03-14 Eng infra sync: Decided to use a single-topic Kafka partitioned by tenant_hash for mapper workers to preserve ordering per tenant and enable per-tenant flow-control. Trade-off: cross-tenant load skew needs autoscaling and per-partition hot-tenant mitigation (thundering herd protection).
testing_plan: Unit tests for envelope serialization and provisional_correlation_id determinism. Integration tests: ingest polymorphic corpus into test cluster, assert mapping accuracy and correlation preservation. Load test: replay 1x and 3x production traffic to validate backpressure behaviour. Canary: enable for internal tenant subset, monitor mapping_error_rate, ingestion_5xx, and tail-latency; proceed on green for 24h.
rollout_plan: 1) Deploy mapper service in staging and run full regression. 2) Canary: 5% traffic (non-critical tenants) for 12h. 3) Observe mapping_success_ratio >= 98% and mapping_error tagging correctness. 4) Ramp to 25% for 48h, then 50% for 48h, monitoring queues and CPU. 5) If any of mapping_error_rate > 1% or ingestion_5xx increases by >0.2pp, rollback to previous routing. Provide post-rollout notes in #observability-alerts.
risks: Hot-tenant skew: single tenant can backfill queue and starve mapper capacity for others
Increased cold-blob egress costs if many tenants opt into raw retention
Edge change could disrupt older agent versions; need backward compatibility and agent feature gate
Mapping rules complexity may still cause edge-case failures leading to noisy error tags
